newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain '98 budget will consolidate recovery - Rato.
newsitem.headline: Spain '98 budget will consolidate recovery - Rato.

text.p: Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday the 1998 budget will keep the Spanish economy on a path of sustained growth.
"The budget for 1998 should consolidate the economic recovery and guarantee macroeconomic stability," Rato told journalists after an informative meeting with unions on the 1998 budget.
The 1998 budget will shape up in such a way "that there is clear margin for monetary policy", Rato said.
For the Economy Minister, tax policy in 1998 will be characterised by sustainability and will resolve structural problems such as health financing.

Rato reiterated that fiscal pressure will be maintained and, at the same time, will guarantee an increase in pensions of 2.1 percent, in line with inflation forecast for 1998. Additional resources will be destined to education.
"The 1998 budget will, without doubt, produce effects that are as positive as those produced by the 1997 one," he added.
He added that there would be no deviations in 1997 accounts. "The 1997 budget wil be the first completed," he said.
